original_answer: The paper does not present head-to-head comparisons against named state-of-the-art summarization systems. Instead, it reports experiments combining semantic models on top of statistical models for extractive summarization [8], using statistical models (TF/IDF, TextRank, Jaccard/Cosine Similarities) and semantic models (WordNet-based, GloVe vectors, Facebook's InferSent), and tests the approach on the DUC 2004 dataset generating 100-word summaries [2]. It mentions that a state-of-the-art abstractive method by Wenyuan Zeng produces summaries of length restricted to 75 [3], and notes that TextRank-based summarization has achieved exemplary benchmark results [11], but the context does not show direct performance comparisons against these approaches. Therefore, based on the provided passages, there is insufficient evidence that they compare against state-of-the-art baselines; the evidence only shows their own model evaluations on DUC 2004 [2] and claims of significant results via tuning weights between models [6].

Though statistical models may better capture word co-occurrences and distribution around the text, they fail to detect the context and the sense of sen- tences /words as a whole. Semantic mod- els help us gain better insight into the con- text of sentences. We show that how tun- ing weights between different models can help us achieve signiﬁcant results on var- ious benchmarks. Learning pre-trained vectors used in semantic models further, on given corpus, can give addition spike in performance.

3.2.2 PageRank PageRank algorithm (Page et al., 1999), devised to rank web pages, forms the core of Google Search. It roughly works by ranking pages accord- ing to the number and quality of outsourcing links from the page. For NLP, a PageRank based tech- nique ,TextRank has been a major breakthrough in the ﬁeld. TextRank based summarization has seeded exemplary results on benchmarks. We use a naive TextRank analogous for our task.
